key_finding: Astera Labs delivered the textbook AI-connectivity print in FY2025: $852.5M revenue (+115% YoY), 75.7% GAAP gross margin (a structural-margin level), $219.1M GAAP net income, $331.0M non-GAAP net income, $319.3M operating cash flow. The Q4 print of $270.6M (+92% YoY, +17% sequential) and the Q1 2026 guide of $286-297M imply continued mid-single-digit sequential growth into the next architecture generation. The balance sheet is fortress: $167.6M cash + $1.02B marketable securities = $1.19B liquid against essentially no debt. The 75.7% GAAP gross margin is the headline — that level of pricing power on small-die semi product is the structural difference between Astera and a typical fabless chip-design business at this scale.

compensation_2025.bonus_metric_split: 50/50 to revenue and non-GAAP operating margin

structural_observations: 75.7% GAAP gross margin in FY2025 places Astera in the top decile of fabless semiconductor companies on margin — a level associated with software more than silicon.
Revenue growing 115% while OpEx grew at a much lower rate is the operating-leverage signature of a connectivity-silicon company moving from design-in to volume.
$1.19B liquid balance sheet against essentially no debt means the company can execute M&A or weather a multi-quarter AI capex pause without near-term financing risk.
Non-GAAP net income $331M vs GAAP $219M — the gap is meaningful and dominated by stock-based compensation, a typical signature of a recently-IPO'd silicon company.
